editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Policies That Cause Massive Damage While Claiming to Protect Citizens
summaryTr: Government policies are causing significant losses under the guise of preventing public harm.
The abolishment of prosecutorial investigative authority, real estate policies, and the introduction of leveraged ETFs have intensified housing insecurity for ordinary citizens.
Regardless of intent, as actual outcomes are worsening people's lives, policy revision is essential.
editorial.bodyTr: This editorial criticizes government policies including the abolition of prosecutorial supplementary investigation authority, real estate policy, and the introduction of single-stock leveraged ETFs, arguing that these measures are actually harming ordinary citizens' lives. It specifically points out concrete side effects such as housing insecurity for low-income households and investment losses for investors, emphasizing that regardless of policy intentions, the actual results are causing damage to the public. The piece stresses the necessity of policy revision.

[청와대사진기자단] 무책임한 발언이라는 지적이 나오자 청와대는 “대통령께서는 형소법 개정의 핵심 내용을 당연히 숙지하고 계신다”고 수습했고, 여권에선 법 개정을 주도한 여당 강경파와 생각이 다르다는 점을 표출한 것이라는 해석이 나왔다. 법안을 숙지하고 문제점을 알면서도 거부권을 안 썼다면 안 읽은 것보다 더 큰 직무유기가 아닌가. 논란을 의식한 듯 이 대통령은 어제 수석보좌관회의에서는 “항상 국민의 눈높이에서 모든 사안을 살피고 문제가 있으면 어떤 사항도 성역 없이 적극적으로 고치는 유연하고 능동적인 행정이 필요하다”고 했다. 대통령의 소신과 발언, 그리고 실제 정책 집행이 다르게 돌아가니 국민만 혼란스러울 뿐이다. 논란을 야기한 검경 합동수사본부 운영에 대한 대통령의 질문에 주무 부처 장관들의 답변이 엇갈린 것도 국민 눈높이에선 어처구니없는 노릇이다. 정성호 법무부 장관은 “검사가 합동 수사할 수 있는 근거는 없다”고 했고, 윤호중 행안부 장관은 “검사가 수사에 관해 의견은 낼 수 있다”고 했다. 70년 넘게 운영된 형사사법 체계를 뒤흔드는 법안이 국회와 국무회의를 통과하는 동안 주무장관들이 가장 기초적인 사안에 대한 입장을 정리하지 못했다는 건 심각한 국정 공백 상황이다. 다수의 국민과 범죄 피해자들까지 뻔히 내다보며 걱정한 사안을 주무장관들은 논의 한 번 안 한 것이기 때문이다. 백번 양보하더라도 이틀 전 국무회의 심의에서는 이견을 정리했어야 할 것 아닌가. 그러니 형소법 개정이 마지막 순간까지 졸속으로 이뤄졌다는 말이 나오는 것이다.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: President Who Hasn't Read Criminal Procedure Act Leaves Cabinet Officials Scrambling Over Interpretation
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung sparks controversy by stating in a cabinet meeting that he has not read the criminal procedure law he passed.
Senior ministers give conflicting answers on prosecutors' investigative authority, exposing a policy vacuum.
Criticism mounts that a bill overturning a 70-year criminal justice system was hastily processed.
editorial.bodyTr: President Lee Jae-myung presided over a cabinet meeting the day before yesterday where statements emerged that made the public question their own ears. The president asked, "I haven't read the revised Criminal Procedure Act, but according to the revised law, is it stipulated that prosecutors cannot conduct investigations?" How can it be that the president had not even read the bill that was decided in the cabinet meeting just 24 hours earlier, despite the opposition of a majority of the people? Moreover, did the president not provide detailed reasons for not exercising his veto power? In that case, judgments such as "it is difficult to view this as a situation serious enough to deny legislative authority" or "an inevitable measure according to the natural course of events" would have been made without reading the bill. When criticism arose about the irresponsible remarks, the Blue House responded by saying, "The president naturally understands the key content of the Criminal Procedure Act revision," and the ruling party offered an interpretation that it expressed a different perspective from the hardliners in the ruling party who led the legal amendment. If the president understood the bill and knew of its problems yet still did not use his veto power, would that not be a greater dereliction of duty than not reading it? As if conscious of the controversy, the president said at a meeting with senior aides yesterday, "We need flexible and proactive administration that always views all matters from the perspective of the people's expectations and actively corrects problems without any sacred cows." Because the president's convictions, statements, and actual policy implementation differ, only the public is left confused. The fact that the answers from relevant cabinet ministers diverged on the president's questions regarding the operation of the joint investigation headquarters between prosecutors and police, which sparked the controversy, is absurd from the public's perspective. Justice Minister Jeong Sung-ho said, "There is no basis for prosecutors to conduct joint investigations," while Interior and Safety Minister Yun Ho-joong said, "Prosecutors can offer opinions regarding investigations." That cabinet ministers failed to clarify their positions on the most fundamental issues while a bill that has shaken the criminal justice system operated for over 70 years passed through the National Assembly and cabinet meeting represents a serious void in state administration. This is because the relevant ministers did not have even one discussion about matters that numerous citizens and crime victims clearly foresaw and worried about. Even if we make a hundred concessions, should they not have organized their differing positions during the cabinet deliberation two days ago? This is why the remark emerged that the Criminal Procedure Act amendment was accomplished hastily until the very last moment.

leanScore.label: Lean progressive
leanScore.rationale: 검찰 수사권 제약 개정을 옹호하면서 대통령과 정부의 무능함을 비판하는 프레이밍으로, 검찰 견제 정책 자체는 지지하되 집행 과정의 부실을 문제 삼음

editorial.title: Leveraged ETF fallout
editorial.body: Korea must restore policy credibility after financial populism fuels market turmoil Markets have a habit of exposing political wishful thinking. They can absorb disappointing earnings and slower growth. They are far less forgiving when governments try to rewrite the rules by which prices are set. South Korea's recent stock market turmoil offers a costly reminder. The catalyst was single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. They debuted in late May as enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence and semiconductor shares approached its peak. Instead of merely amplifying investor interest, the products intensified every subsequent decline. Violent swings through June and July triggered automatic liquidations, repeated trading halts and heavy losses for retail investors. Regulators later tightened investment requirements and suspended additional launches, sharply reducing trading activity. Those emergency steps calmed speculation, yet they arrived only after the damage had spread. Many have portrayed the turmoil as another chapter in the global technology correction or the semiconductor cycle. Those forces clearly mattered. But they do not explain why Korea’s benchmark index became one of the world's most turbulent major equity markets within weeks. The answer lies partly in market structure. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix already dominate the benchmark index. Introducing derivatives that doubled daily price movements concentrated even greater pressure on an already narrow market. Daily portfolio rebalancing and margin requirements then reinforced each decline. Falling prices prompted forced selling, which drove prices lower and generated fresh liquidations, creating a feedback loop that spread well beyond the semiconductor sector. What began as a correction in a handful of stocks distorted price formation across the broader market. This turned an ordinary downturn into a painful breakdown in market stability. The authorities' response inadvertently made the point. They accelerated plans to raise the minimum cash deposit from 10 million won ($7,050) to 30 million won, examined portfolio exposure limits and halted new listings of similar products. Those measures were sensible. They also suggested that safeguards deserved closer scrutiny before the products ever reached investors. Equally troubling is the speed with which such a consequential policy reached the market. Opposition parties have demanded investigations, while criticism has spread beyond partisan lines. Even figures broadly aligned with the Lee Jae Myung administration have called for a closer examination of the approval process for the leveraged ETFs. The issue extends beyond one financial product. Transparent decision-making is essential because trust in financial supervision depends as much on institutional independence as regulatory expertise. When policy initiatives appear to originate in political offices while regulators adjust course afterward, the boundary between oversight and political direction inevitably becomes blurred. Foreign media’s portrayal of Korea as an unpredictable investment destination may overstate the case, and government officials are right to point to robust exports, healthy corporate earnings and solid macroeconomic indicators. Yet sound fundamentals cannot fully offset doubts created when financial rules appear vulnerable to shifting political priorities rather than consistent regulatory judgment. That distinction matters because the “Korea discount” has never reflected corporate performance alone. Investors evaluate the credibility of policymaking. Sudden regulatory shifts, emergency interventions and uncertainty over who ultimately directs financial oversight inevitably raise the premium global investors demand. A transparent review of how single-stock leveraged ETFs won approval would therefore strengthen the market rather than weaken it. It should clarify whether internal objections received adequate consideration and whether institutional safeguards functioned as intended. Speculative enthusiasm can lift share prices for a time, but lasting gains depend on institutional credibility. The government is moving to stabilize markets and rebuild confidence. Assuming belated measures can quickly restore trust would itself be another form of political wishful thinking. 시장은 정치적 희망사항을 드러내는 습성이 있다. 시장은 실망스러운 실적과 둔화된 성장률을 흡수할 수 있다. 그러나 정부가 가격이 결정되는 규칙을 다시 쓰려고 할 때는 훨씬 덜 관용적이다. 한국의 최근 주식시장 혼란은 이를 비용이 많이 드는 교훈으로 제시한다. 촉발 요인은 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스와 연계된 단일종목 레버리지 상장지수펀드(ETF)였다. 이들은 인공지능과 반도체 주식에 대한 열정이 정점에 이르렀던 5월 말 출시됐다. 이 상품들은 투자자의 관심을 단순히 증폭시키는 대신 그 이후의 모든 하락을 심화시켰다. 6월과 7월을 통한 급격한 변동은 자동 청산, 반복되는 거래 중단, 그리고 개인투자자들에게 상당한 손실을 초래했다. 규제당국은 이후 투자 요건을 강화하고 추가 출시를 중단하며 거래 활동을 급격히 감소시켰다. 이러한 긴급 조치는 투기를 진정시켰으나 손실이 이미 광범위하게 확산된 후에야 실행됐다.

많은 사람들이 이 혼란을 글로벌 기술 조정이나 반도체 사이클의 또 다른 장으로 묘사했다. 이러한 요인들이 분명히 중요했다. 하지만 한국의 벤치마크 지수가 수주 내에 세계에서 가장 변동성이 큰 주요 주식시장 중 하나가 된 이유를 설명하지는 못한다. 그 답은 부분적으로 시장 구조에 있다. 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스는 이미 벤치마크 지수를 지배하고 있다. 일일 가격 변동을 두 배로 하는 파생상품을 도입함으로써 이미 좁은 시장에 훨씬 더 큰 압력이 집중됐다. 일일 포트폴리오 리밸런싱과 증거금 요건이 이후의 모든 하락을 강화했다. 가격 하락으로 인한 강제 매도가 가격을 더욱 낮추고 새로운 청산을 발생시켜 반도체 부문을 훨씬 넘어서 확산되는 악순환을 만들었다. 소수의 주식에서 시작된 조정이 더 광범위한 시장의 가격 형성을 왜곡했다. 이는 평범한 하락을 시장 안정성의 고통스러운 붕괴로 전환시켰다.

당국의 대응은 의도하지 않게 이 점을 강조했다. 최소 현금보증금을 1천만 원에서 3천만 원으로 인상할 계획을 가속화하고, 포트폴리오 익스포저 한도를 검토하고, 유사 상품의 신규 상장을 중단했다. 이러한 조치는 합리적이었다. 또한 이는 안전장치가 상품이 투자자에게 도달하기 전에 더 긴밀한 검토를 받아야 했음을 시사했다. 그만큼 우려스러운 것은 이러한 중대한 정책이 시장에 도달한 신속함이다. 야당은 조사를 요구했고, 비판은 당파적 범위를 넘어 확산됐다. 이준석 행정부와 광범위하게 일치하는 인물들도 레버리지 ETF 승인 절차에 대한 더 자세한 검토를 촉구했다.

문제는 하나의 금융 상품을 넘어선다. 금융 감시에 대한 신뢰는 규제 전문성만큼이나 제도적 독립성에 달려 있기 때문에 투명한 의사결정이 필수적이다. 정책 발의가 정치 사무실에서 비롯된 것처럼 보이고 규제당국이 나중에 방침을 조정하면, 감시와 정치적 방향 사이의 경계는 필연적으로 모호해진다. 외신이 한국을 예측 불가능한 투자처로 묘사한 것은 과장된 면이 있을 수 있으며, 정부 관계자들이 견고한 수출, 건전한 기업 실적, 견실한 거시경제 지표를 지적하는 것은 타당하다. 그러나 건전한 기초는 금융 규칙이 일관된 규제 판단보다는 변화하는 정치적 우선순위에 취약해 보일 때 발생하는 의심을 완전히 상쇄할 수 없다. 이 구별이 중요한 이유는 "한국 할인"이 기업 성과만을 반영한 적이 없기 때문이다. 투자자들은 정책 결정의 신뢰성을 평가한다. 갑작스러운 규제 변화, 긴급 개입, 누가 궁극적으로 금융 감시를 지휘하는지에 대한 불확실성은 필연적으로 글로벌 투자자들이 요구하는 프리미엄을 높인다.

따라서 단일종목 레버리지 ETF가 승인된 방식을 투명하게 검토하면 시장을 약화시키기보다는 강화할 것이다. 내부 반대가 적절한 고려를 받았는지, 제도적 안전장치가 의도대로 작동했는지를 명확히 해야 한다. 투기적 열정은 한때 주가를 올릴 수 있지만, 지속적인 이득은 제도적 신뢰성에 달려 있다. 정부는 시장을 안정화하고 신뢰를 회복하기 위해 움직이고 있다. 지연된 조치가 신속하게 신뢰를 회복할 수 있다고 가정하는 것 자체가 또 다른 형태의 정치적 희망사항일 것이다.

editorials.title: Leveraged ETF fallout
editorials.body: Korea must restore policy credibility after financial populism fuels market turmoil Markets have a habit of exposing political wishful thinking. They can absorb disappointing earnings and slower growth. They are far less forgiving when governments try to rewrite the rules by which prices are set. South Korea's recent stock market turmoil offers a costly reminder. The catalyst was single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. They debuted in late May as enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence and semiconductor shares approached its peak. Instead of merely amplifying investor interest, the products intensified every subsequent decline. Violent swings through June and July triggered automatic liquidations, repeated trading halts and heavy losses for retail investors. Regulators later tightened investment requirements and suspended additional launches, sharply reducing trading activity. Those emergency steps calmed speculation, yet they arrived only after the damage had spread. Many have portrayed the turmoil as another chapter in the global technology correction or the semiconductor cycle. Those forces clearly mattered. But they do not explain why Korea’s benchmark index became one of the world's most turbulent major equity markets within weeks. The answer lies partly in market structure. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix already dominate the benchmark index. Introducing derivatives that doubled daily price movements concentrated even greater pressure on an already narrow market. Daily portfolio rebalancing and margin requirements then reinforced each decline. Falling prices prompted forced selling, which drove prices lower and generated fresh liquidations, creating a feedback loop that spread well beyond the semiconductor sector. What began as a correction in a handful of stocks distorted price formation across the broader market. This turned an ordinary downturn into a painful breakdown in market stability. The authorities' response inadvertently made the point. They accelerated plans to raise the minimum cash deposit from 10 million won ($7,050) to 30 million won, examined portfolio exposure limits and halted new listings of similar products. Those measures were sensible. They also suggested that safeguards deserved closer scrutiny before the products ever reached investors. Equally troubling is the speed with which such a consequential policy reached the market. Opposition parties have demanded investigations, while criticism has spread beyond partisan lines. Even figures broadly aligned with the Lee Jae Myung administration have called for a closer examination of the approval process for the leveraged ETFs. The issue extends beyond one financial product. Transparent decision-making is essential because trust in financial supervision depends as much on institutional independence as regulatory expertise. When policy initiatives appear to originate in political offices while regulators adjust course afterward, the boundary between oversight and political direction inevitably becomes blurred. Foreign media’s portrayal of Korea as an unpredictable investment destination may overstate the case, and government officials are right to point to robust exports, healthy corporate earnings and solid macroeconomic indicators. Yet sound fundamentals cannot fully offset doubts created when financial rules appear vulnerable to shifting political priorities rather than consistent regulatory judgment. That distinction matters because the “Korea discount” has never reflected corporate performance alone. Investors evaluate the credibility of policymaking. Sudden regulatory shifts, emergency interventions and uncertainty over who ultimately directs financial oversight inevitably raise the premium global investors demand. A transparent review of how single-stock leveraged ETFs won approval would therefore strengthen the market rather than weaken it. It should clarify whether internal objections received adequate consideration and whether institutional safeguards functioned as intended. Speculative enthusiasm can lift share prices for a time, but lasting gains depend on institutional credibility. The government is moving to stabilize markets and rebuild confidence. Assuming belated measures can quickly restore trust would itself be another form of political wishful thinking.
